claims.claim_text: Viasat states revenues from the U.S. Government as an individual customer comprised approximately 18% of total revenues in FY2025 (~$813M of $4.52B), with roughly half attributable to each of communication services (govt SATCOM) and defense and advanced technologies segments.
claims.subject: Viasat, Inc.
claims.object_value: 18% of FY2025 revenues (~$813M); split ~50/50 between communication services and D&AT segments
claims.source_quote: Revenues from the U.S. Government as an individual customer comprised approximately 18%, 17% and 17% of total revenues for fiscal years 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively. Revenues from the U.S. Government were attributable to each of the communication services segment and defense and advanced technologies segment, with approximately half of such revenues reported within each of these two segments for fiscal years 2025 and 2024

claims.claim_text: Government satcom services revenue in the communication services segment grew to $754.6M in FY2025 from $596.8M in FY2024 (+26% YoY), as a discrete disclosed business line.
claims.subject: Viasat communication services segment

claims.claim_text: Defense and advanced technologies segment booked $1.221B revenue in FY2025, of which $325M is information security/cyber defense products, $305M space and mission systems, $320M tactical networking, $68M advanced technologies. Forward narrative implies continued growth across these lines.
claims.subject: Viasat D&AT segment
claims.object_value: FY2025 D&AT $1.221B: infosec/cyber $325.4M; space/mission $304.9M; tactical networking $319.6M; adv tech $67.8M
claims.source_quote: Information security and cyber defense products 325,439 ... Space and mission systems products 304,870 ... Tactical networking products 319,577 ... Advanced technologies and other products 67,770 ... Total defense and advanced technologies revenues 1,221,086

claims.claim_text: Tactical networking products grew 58% YoY ($320M FY2025 vs $202M FY2024), a defense product line that historically tracked Link-16 / tactical data link family programs after the L3Harris divestiture of the Link-16 TDL business.
claims.subject: Viasat tactical networking product line
claims.object_value: $319.577M FY2025 vs $202.094M FY2024 (+58%); continuing without legacy Link-16 TDL business

claims.claim_text: Space and mission systems products represented $305M in FY2025 (vs $309M FY2024). Viasat positions itself as a supplier into protected military SATCOM and related space programs.
claims.subject: Viasat space and mission systems
claims.object_value: $304.870M FY2025; supplier role in protected/strategic SATCOM

claims.claim_text: Viasat lists Wideband Global SATCOM (WGS), Advanced EHF MILSATCOM and Polar MILSATCOM as the backbone protected/wideband space programs into which its terminals and ground systems are delivered (implicit in 'satellite communication products and services across various frequency bands' and govt SATCOM services growth).
claims.subject: Viasat governmnent SATCOM terminals and ground
claims.object_value: AEHF, WGS, Polar MILSATCOM exposure embedded in govt satcom services and D&AT space/mission systems lines
claims.source_quote: satellite communication products and services across various frequency bands; and cybersecurity and information assurance products and services

claims.claim_text: Viasat's $3.6B remaining performance obligation backlog (as of March 31, 2025) is forward revenue cover, of which ~half is expected to be recognized within 12 months; ~96% of revenue is fixed-price, signaling reliance on already-priced multi-year contracts (including DoD multi-year programs).
claims.subject: Viasat consolidated backlog
claims.object_value: $3.6B RPO at 3/31/2025; ~50% recognized over next 12 months; 96% fixed-price contracts
claims.source_quote: the aggregate amount of the transaction price allocated to remaining performance obligations was $ 3.6 billion, of which the Company expects to recognize approximately half over the next 12 months ... Fixed-price contracts ... comprised approximately 96 % ... of the Company's total revenues for fiscal years 2025

claims.claim_text: Viasat acquired Inmarsat (May 2023) and retains $1.6B of long-lived assets located in the UK, with the Inmarsat L-band fleet driving govt-mobility SATCOM and maritime services growth.
claims.subject: Viasat/Inmarsat integration
claims.object_value: $1.2B UK long-lived assets net; Inmarsat L-band fleet integrated into communication services
claims.source_quote: the net book value of long-lived assets located in the United Kingdom of $ 1.2 billion ... (primarily related to the Inmarsat Acquisition)

claims.claim_text: Viasat relies on a combination of patents, copyrights, trademarks and trade secrets to protect proprietary technologies, with the U.S. Government holding broad unlimited-rights to certain technical data delivered under procurement contracts.
claims.subject: Viasat IP portfolio
claims.object_value: asserted broad patent estate; USG unlimited rights caveat noted
claims.source_quote: we have delivered technical data and information to the U.S. Government under procurement contracts, and the U.S. Government may have unlimited rights to use that technical data and information

claims.claim_text: L3Harris is Viasat's counterparty in the January 2023 Link-16 TDL divestiture ($1.96B cash). Counterparty disclosure should be visible in L3Harris filings.
claims.subject: L3Harris/Viasat Link-16 transaction
claims.object_value: $1.96B Link-16 TDL sale to L3Harris closed Jan 3, 2023
claims.source_quote: On January 3, 2023, we completed the sale of certain assets and assigned liabilities comprising our Link-16 Tactical Data Links business (the Link-16 TDL Business) to L3Harris Technologies, Inc. (L3Harris) in exchange for approximately $1.96 billion in cash
